decisions.decision: The red criterion is now: the red you hand forward must have RUN and failed, with the failure originating in the code under test rather than in module load, collection or setup. An assertion failure is the sharpest form; a not-implemented throw or an in-body error is valid but blunter; a build or import failure is a prerequisite to clear. Characterization tests are carved out as green by construction.
decisions.rationale: Owner-approved. FOUR owned sources independently decline to require an AssertionError specifically: Clean Code (a build failure IS a legitimate red), Beck (clear the compile error, then run and fail; his own canonical stub throws), Fowler Refactoring 2e Ch.4 (failure versus error, the boundary being an earlier phase), and Meszaros (an error is a legitimate, equally severe red you are told NOT to convert into a failure).

decisions.decision: Step 2 was KEPT and scoped, not deleted.
decisions.rationale: Its missing-symbol clause is true about Law 2, which governs when to stop WRITING the test, and it is owned and oracle-verified to Clean Code. The contradiction was two questions sharing the word failure. The fix disambiguates rather than picking a winner.

decisions.rationale: Meszaros is the reference frame for the collaborator-side term set only. He is explicitly denied production-side, valid-red and Beck-interpretation authority: he never names the SUT-side transitional artifact, his outcome vocabulary has no slot for a non-running test, and his Beck-to-Fake mapping carries no page, no note and no discussion of Fake It anywhere in the volume.

decisions.rationale: TWELVE authors checked, none names it. placeholder is ruled out from BOTH sides -- Meszaros registers it as a Dummy Object alias and GoF used it production-side in 1994. Bare stub is unusable because owned sources claim it for opposite cells. Kerievsky's skeleton was the only owned candidate. Meszaros' own Self Shunt naming self-criticism is the disclosure model.

decisions.decision: Duplicate the taxonomy byte-identical into all three skills rather than sharing one copy.
decisions.rationale: Tier-1 evidence: the Anthropic engineering blog scopes bundled files to within the skill directory; agentskills.io/specification says use relative paths from the skill root; anthropics/skills stores byte-identical copies with zero symlinks. Duplication costs ZERO extra context since only the invoked skill's copy is read. A sha256 byte-identity gate makes it safe. Consequence: the document can carry no markdown link containing a slash, because the three skills' sibling trees differ.

Its only skeleton is Template Method's algorithm outline, which would be a misread if cited for the RPC sense. Replaced with an owned chronology: production-side stand-in vocabulary documented at 1994 with lineage credited back to 1963, versus a 2007 test-double vocabulary.

decisions.decision: Agent worktrees are now git-ignored, and teardown is by exact path then exact branch name.
decisions.rationale: .claude/worktrees/ was NOT ignored and held a 78 MB second checkout. The nested checkout's own .gitignore already covered .oracle/ and .continue-here.md, so the exposure was bulk rather than sensitive. Order matters: git branch -d refuses while the branch is checked out in a worktree, so remove the worktree FIRST.

context_notes: EIGHT of my own errors were caught this session, most of them by the user or by a subagent rather than by my own inspection. (1) I dispatched the executor while the planner was STILL RUNNING, creating a race that nearly cost five real plan requirements -- wait for a planner to return before committing its plan. (2) I invoked three checkers from the wrong workspace and briefly read a module-resolution crash as a gate failure; check-backing, check-crossrefs and check-hygiene live in lz-refactor-workspace, NOT lz-red-workspace -- locate each with find before running. (3) I asserted an unowned RPC etymology and had to retract it; the user's question about GoF is the only reason it was caught before shipping, and it caught it by inverting my own reasoning -- I had excluded GoF BECAUSE it predates the taxonomy, which is exactly what made it worth consulting. (4) I claimed .claude/skills/ is gitignored; the checker is tracked (git check-ignore exits 1). (5) I inferred the placeholder scaffold ban must be narrower than the bare word because the word appears in the tree -- wrong, the ban IS on the bare word and the existing occurrence escapes only because the plural breaks the trailing word boundary. Read the regex instead of inferring from an apparent contradiction. (6) I predicted the book would be materially fuller on Overspecified Software; it is the same single paragraph, so the site reproduced the book's own layout. (7) My teardown script printed 'retrying with --force' from a || branch that only echoed and never forced -- a script that CLAIMS it escalated while doing nothing is the same false-signal pattern as the failing gates. (8) I had the teardown order wrong: git branch -d refused not because the branch was unmerged (I had proven it an ancestor of HEAD) but because it was still CHECKED OUT in the worktree, shown by the + prefix in git branch -vv. Worktree first, then branch. SEPARATELY the executor found a GUARD THAT COULD NEVER FIRE: a per-line absent regex against a stale marker that WRAPS across two lines reported PASS while the text was fully present. Third false-GREEN of the session. Always verify a new guard FAILS at baseline before trusting it. FINALLY, and most important: the taxonomy is 310 lines and NOBODY has read it end to end, including me. I verified it mechanically -- sha256 byte-identity across three copies, zero fences, zero slash-bearing links, ASCII, email allowlist-inversion -- but not substantively. That is precisely what the unbiased review is for, and it is why gates-green must not be mistaken for accepted. Four prior proposals in this milestone died to gates and none to inspection.
